introduction: South Carolina TANF helps qualifying families with children. Caretaker relatives should ask whether a child-only grant or a grant including the adult fits their situation.
description: South Carolina TANF helps qualifying families with children. Caretaker relatives should ask whether a child-only grant or a grant including the adult fits their situation.

sections.who: DSS assesses low-income family circumstances, qualifying relationships and status. Child-support cooperation and adult participation requirements can apply.
sections.get: Approved cash and related employment support help meet family needs. Adult benefit-group membership affects the financial assessment.

sections.apply:
1. Apply through DSS

    Use the portal or county-office routes.

  2. Discuss the benefit group

    Caretaker relatives should ask about child-only treatment and relevant child income.

  3. Complete the plan

    Review your decision and any work or child-support instructions.
sections.after: Keep records and report changes through county-office routes. Ask about a child’s other payments before assuming TANF can be combined.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Caretaker-relative rules and case contact, Application routes, Eligibility and participation. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Does my income count in a child-only relative grant?
DSS says caregiver income and resources do not affect that child-only grant, but certain child income can count.
Can some other child payments prevent TANF?
DSS lists SSI and specified foster, guardianship, adoption or kinship payments as exclusions.
Can I request a mailed form?
DSS lists 800-616-1309 for mailed application or renewal forms.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
